name: Opus 5 pairs
strategy: Six market-neutral relative-value pairs (WFC/BAC, TSM/KLAC, LOW/HD, MA/V, XLU/D and QUAL+IWF vs MTUM) chosen from a 150-symbol screen for a stretched 250-day log-spread z-score AND evidence of stationarity - at least 8 crossings of the spread's own mean in the past year, under 25% two-year drift and above 0.60 daily-return correlation - with each pair sized so its long and short betas cancel, leaving net SPY beta of +3.2% of NAV.

positions.thesis: Long leg vs BAC, raised from 18.5 because the spread got more stretched on the measure I actually underwrote. WFC at roughly $87.5 still sits ~10% below its $97.76 52-week high with a $100.02 consensus target implying 14.3% upside, while BAC just printed a fresh high; the convergence gap is now 7.2 points versus 5.7 a week ago. This remains the best stationarity evidence anywhere in my universe — 17 mean-crossings in a year, near-zero two-year drift, 0.80 daily-return correlation, betas 0.76 vs 0.77 — and 12.7x trailing against BAC's ~14.6x is what carries the reversion. The week's news was confirmatory rather than new: stress test passed with the stress capital buffer held at 2.5%, dividend going to $0.50, and membership in the Clearing House tokenized-deposit consortium. Both banks reported 07-14 so there is no calendar event inside my horizon. I accept that at 41.8% of gross this pair is over half the book's risk, which is why I stopped at 21.0 rather than pushing further.

Short leg vs WFC, sized 20.8 against 21.0 so the 0.77 and 0.76 betas cancel to within 0.06% of NAV. Nothing has gone wrong with BAC and that continues to be the entire point: Q2 EPS of $1.21 beat $1.12 by 8%, Global Markets revenue rose 34% to $8.02bn, investment banking fees rose 50%, and Moynihan says pipelines are strong. The stock has responded by taking out a 52-week high at $65.20 and compressing its own consensus upside to 7.1% against a $68.77 target. I am short the price of an excellent franchise at the point where the sell side has almost no room left, not the franchise itself. The risk I own here is that a genuinely accelerating capital-markets cycle keeps re-rating BAC past the sell side, which is exactly why this is a beta-cancelled spread and not an outright short.

Long leg vs KLAC, held unchanged. TSM closed 08-14 at $430.49, still ~10% below its $479 52-week high, with 18 buys and no sells and a $547.09 average target implying 27% upside — it continues to lag the sector it physically manufactures for. The screen showed the largest convergence in my universe, ~19% back to the 250-day mean with a 34-day half-life, 15 mean-crossings and only -12% two-year drift, so last year's relative fall reads as oscillation rather than decay. I do not add despite the week's gain because the evidence on the short leg moved both ways, and resizing one side of a beta-matched pair on ambiguous information is how a spread quietly becomes a directional semis bet.

Short leg vs TSM, held at 6.4 against an 8.0 long because KLAC's 2.70 beta exceeds TSM's 2.15 — beta-matched, not dollar-matched. KLAC closed $203.72, down 2.70% on 08-14, at 55.7x trailing with a $231.78 target leaving 13.8% upside against TSM's 27%. I state the evidence against myself plainly: Lam guided calendar-2026 wafer-fab equipment to the low $150bn range versus a prior ~$140bn, which means the cycle peak I claimed KLAC was pricing is higher than I assumed. What keeps the leg on is the market's own answer — Applied Materials fell 6% premarket on 08-14 despite record revenue and a 51% growth guide. When a group cannot rally on its best possible news, the multiple is the binding constraint. This stays my smallest and most violent spread on purpose; shorting semi-cap into an AI capex boom remains the position most likely to be wrong for the longest.

Long leg vs HD, restored from 9.0 to 11.0 because the specific condition I trimmed on last week has been removed. I cut this pair when consensus upside had converged to roughly 14% for LOW against 15% for HD — no edge worth paying an earnings window for. After this week's selloff LOW sits at $218.47, near its $199.40 52-week low, with a $261.06 target implying 19.5% upside against HD's 10.4%: a 9.1-point gap where there was effectively none. The hedge quality is unchanged and second only to WFC/BAC — 0.88 daily-return correlation, betas 0.65 vs 0.68, 16 mean-crossings, only -6% two-year drift. LOW reports 08-19 pre-open with consensus at ~$26.2bn revenue and adj EPS ~$4.24 versus $4.33 a year ago, i.e. guided down on acquisition costs, comps around +1%, and FY26 reaffirmed at $92-94bn with $12.25-12.75 EPS. That is a low bar on a de-rated price, which is the asymmetry I want on the long side of a two-day print window.

Short leg vs LOW, sized 10.5 against 11.0 so the 0.68 and 0.65 betas cancel to within 0.01% of NAV. HD closed $338.86 and reports 08-18 pre-open, one day before LOW — which is precisely what makes this pair worth carrying through rather than flattening: two near-identical retailers reporting 24 hours apart means the common housing shock, mortgage rates near 6.5% and turnover at multi-year lows, lands on both sets of numbers and leaves the execution difference I am actually betting on. HD's setup is the harder one: consensus wants revenue ~$47.5bn and EPS $4.71 versus $4.68, i.e. growth, against freshly raised targets from BofA at $412 and TD Cowen at $410 that still leave only 10.4% upside. New this week and specific to this leg, CEO Ted Decker is on temporary medical leave with the CFO and an EVP covering — a governance and execution question at exactly the wrong moment in a duopoly where execution is the bet. I carry no stop on this leg: stopping out one side of a beta-matched pair would leave me naked long LOW into its own print.

reassessment_note: Weekly desk 2026-08-15: Two of my five spreads stopped qualifying this week for opposite reasons, and the reason I trimmed a third was erased by new information. MA/V hit its exit condition: MA rose 15% on a clean Q2 (net revenue +14%, adj EPS $5.04 vs $4.77, guidance raised) and the target-implied gap that got me in collapsed from 9 points to 2.6. A mandate built on stationary spreads takes the convergence when it arrives; holding on hoping a mean-reverting spread overshoots is not the trade I described, and MA's move was earnings, not noise, so I will not flip the sign either. The factor triangle goes to zero because I already conceded its thesis was falsified — I underwrote momentum's excess as crowding and MU/AMD/AVGO delivered earnings instead — and a residual short of a thesis I no longer believe is just a slow leak, which it proved again this week (MTUM +2.55% vs IWF +0.55%). The November reconstitution will also drag MTUM's beta toward Micron's ~2.2 against the ~1.5 my triangle is matched to, and I cannot re-hedge drift from inside a fund; better to own no beta mismatch than a small one I cannot fix. Against that I add to the two spreads whose evidence improved. WFC/BAC widened against me on price while widening in my favour on substance: BAC printed a fresh 52-week high at $65.20 and its consensus upside fell to 7.1% while WFC's held at 14.3%, so the convergence gap went from 5.7 to 7.2 points on the book's best stationarity evidence (17 mean-crossings, ~zero two-year drift, 0.80 correlation). LOW/HD is the honest reversal: last week I cut it from 21.5% of gross precisely because consensus upside had converged to ~14% vs ~15% and I refused to pay for a two-day earnings window with no edge in it. That gap is now 9.1 points (LOW +19.5% with the stock near its 52-week low, HD +10.4% on freshly RAISED targets), LOW's bar into the print is lower (EPS guided down yoy on deal costs), and HD's CEO is on medical leave. The condition that justified the trim is gone, so I restore the size rather than pretend consistency means never changing back. TSM/KLAC stays exactly where it is because the week cut both ways — Lam lifting CY2026 WFE to the low $150bns says the cycle peak is higher than my short assumed, while AMAT dropping 6% on record revenue and a 51% growth guide says the multiple, not the fundamentals, is the binding constraint. Mixed evidence is a reason to hold a position, not to resize it. Gross falls from 90.5% to 77.7% and cash rises to 22.3%: I cut two sub-books and found no replacement that passed my screen — XLU/D is now a merger-arb instrument because of the NextEra deal, CVX/XOM trade at identical forward multiples, GS/MS is a one-point gap — so the unused gross earns 4% instead of buying a spread I have not measured. I attach no stops or take-profits anywhere: on a beta-matched pair a per-leg percentage stop is triggered by the market's direction rather than the spread's, and firing one leg converts a hedged relative-value position into an outright directional bet, which is a worse outcome than the loss it was meant to cap. Everything fills at the next open — I want the MA/V convergence banked before it can give back, and the LOW/HD size on before the 08-18 print.
novelty: Not applicable in substance since I run no Round-2 book, but for the record this Round 3 book is now three intra-industry single-stock pairs — WFC/BAC, TSM/KLAC, LOW/HD — with zero ETF, index or factor exposure after retiring the IWF/QUAL/MTUM triangle and the MA/V payments spread, so it shares no same-direction gross weight with any factor- or index-based construction.
research_notes:
Packet first: Round 3 only (I run no Round-2 book), NAV $1,003.82, +0.38%, max DD -0.71%, gross 90.5%, cash 9.45%, book entered 2026-08-10. No standing orders were attached, so nothing fired; every leg is still at its entry weight.

Marked all ten legs through the 2026-08-14 close and, more importantly, re-checked the evidence each spread was underwritten on.

WFC/BAC — WFC ~$87.5 (consensus $100.02, +14.28%); BAC $64.2 area, closed 08-14 in a $63.81-$64.52 range with a fresh 52-week high of $65.20 and a consensus target of $68.77 (+7.1%). Price moved against me (BAC +1.6% vs WFC +0.3%) but the analyst-implied convergence gap WIDENED from 5.7 points to 7.2. BAC's Q2 was genuinely good (EPS $1.21 vs $1.12, markets revenue +34%, IB fees +50%) — I am short the price of that quality, not the franchise, and the price got dearer. WFC news was confirmatory: stress test passed with a 2.5% SCB, dividend to $0.50, tokenized-deposit consortium. Both reported 07-14, calendar clear.

TSM/KLAC — TSM $430.49 (+2.5% on the week), 52w high $479, target $547.09 (+27%), 18 buys/0 sells. KLAC closed $203.72, -2.70% on 08-14, 55.7x trailing, target $231.78 (+13.8%). Evidence is genuinely two-sided this week: Lam's CEO raised CY2026 WFE to the low-$150bn range from ~$140bn, which makes the cycle peak higher than my short assumed — that is a point against me. Against that, AMAT fell 6% premarket on 08-14 despite record revenue and a 51% growth guide, and KLAC sold off with it. The group is being told that good news is already in the multiple. Mixed evidence, so I do not resize.

LOW/HD — the biggest change in the book. LOW $218.47, sitting near its 52w low of $199.40 after a week's selloff, target $261.06 = +19.5%. HD $338.86, target $374.06 = +10.4%, with BofA ($412) and TD Cowen ($410) actually RAISING targets, so the gap is not a stale-estimate artifact. The consensus-upside gap I trimmed on last week — LOW ~14% vs HD ~15%, i.e. roughly nothing — has re-opened to 9.1 points in favour of my long. Separately, HD disclosed that CEO Ted Decker is on temporary medical leave with CFO McPhail and an EVP covering — an execution question that lands on the short leg. Setups into the prints: HD 08-18 pre-open, consensus ~$47.5bn and EPS $4.71 vs $4.68 (up yoy); LOW 08-19 pre-open, ~$26.2bn and adj EPS ~$4.24 vs $4.33 (down yoy on acquisition costs), comps guided ~+1%, FY26 reaffirmed at $92-94bn and $12.25-12.75. LOW carries the lower bar and the cheaper entry.

MA/V — the pair converged violently and is done. MA $569.29 vs $493.98 a week ago (+15%) on a Q2 beat: net revenue +14% to $9.3bn, adj EPS $5.04 vs $4.77 est, net income $4.4bn (+19%), guidance to the high end, plus Ackman's agentic-commerce position. V $364.15, only 2.7% below its 52w high. The target-implied gap I entered on has collapsed from 9 points (MA +31% vs V +22%) to 2.6 points (MA +16.9% vs V +14.3%). The z-score has reverted; that is the exit condition, not a reason to press.

Factor triangle — MTUM $317.21 (+2.55%), IWF $125.29 (+0.55%). The spread went against me a third straight week. MTUM's top three are still MU 6.18%, AMD 4.93%, AVGO 4.80% — the earnings inflection I admitted last week had falsified my crowding thesis.

Replacement candidates screened and rejected: XLU/D, named in my own mandate, is now uninvestable as a spread — Dominion is inside a proposed $66.8bn NextEra merger with the Virginia governor pledging to intervene, so D trades on deal odds, and both D and NEE (13% of XLU) sit inside the ETF. CVX $200.00 (+8.5% upside, 13.25x fwd) vs XOM $160.10 (+5.3%, 13.18x fwd) — forward multiples are effectively identical, no dislocation. GS $1,039.42 (16.1x, +10%) vs MS $217.36 (17.6x, +8.9%) — a one-point gap is not a stretched z-score. Nothing else cleared the screen, so freed gross goes to cash at 4% rather than into a pair I have not screened.

Resulting net SPY beta: WFC/BAC -0.06%, TSM/KLAC -0.08%, LOW/HD +0.01% — about -0.13% of NAV, i.e. flat, versus the +3.2% residual the prior configuration carried.
